item.title: The Voice Winner Bryce Leatherwood of Woodstock, Georgia Is Back With 'Beers and Ballads': What to Know
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Woodstock, Georgia's Bryce Leatherwood, winner of The Voice season 22, releases Beers and Ballads, a 10-track country album, on Sept. 18, 2026.
item.content:encoded:
Blake Shelton's final Voice champion follows his 2025 Mercury Nashville debut with Beers and Ballads, a 10-track album out Sept. 18, 2026.

Woodstock, Georgia country singer Bryce Leatherwood, the season 22 winner of The Voice, is back with Beers and Ballads, set for release Sept. 18, 2026, according to its Spotify, Audiomack, and iHeart listings. The 10-track album follows his self-titled debut, which Mercury Nashville released on May 16, 2025, per Wikipedia.

The track list opens with "D-R-I-N-K-I-N-G" and runs through "She's Wrong, She's Right," "Grain of Salt," "I'd Be Dammed," "Let Me Have This Dance" and "One More Day (Closer to Hell)" before the title track closes it out.

Blake Shelton's last Voice win

Leatherwood won season 22 on Dec. 13, 2022, as a member of Team Blake. According to Wikipedia, he was the first winner of the show to be a Wildcard artist during the live playoffs, and it was Shelton's ninth and final win as a coach. The prize included $100,000 and a record deal with Universal Music Group.

Born Feb. 4, 2000, and raised in Woodstock, he released his debut country radio single, "Hung Up on You," on Sept. 6, 2024. He made his Grand Ole Opry debut on Sept. 14, singing that song and the then-unreleased "Shenandoah." "Hung Up on You" peaked at No. 56 on Country Airplay.

Grandpa's farm and Conway Twitty

"My grandfather had me working on his farm in Macon, Georgia, while teaching me about classic country and Southern rock," he told American Songwriter. After singing in church, he listened to Conway Twitty songs in his grandfather's truck. The magazine also names George Jones and Merle Haggard among his childhood listening.

Growing up in North Georgia surrounded by mountains shaped his debut. He said he wanted to "carry that inspiration into a song that reminded me of home."

What critics heard last time

Saving Country Music reviewed the debut and wrote that "the sound is certainly country," calling it "more early 2000s traditional country" and noting that Will Bundy's production isn't exactly the hot '90s country sound. The site scored it 7 out of 10 and called "The Finger" quite clever.

Wikipedia lists "The Finger," performed on The Voice in December 2023, as his first major label single, followed by "Neon Does" and "The One My Daddy Found" in 2024. He launched the Neon Does Tour through several southern and midwestern states in April 2024 and has played Shelton's Ole Red bar chain in Tishomingo, Oklahoma; Orlando, Florida; and Gatlinburg, Tennessee.

What's still unknown

Streaming listings for Beers and Ballads credit Sony Music Publishing (US) LLC and do not name a record label, so YourInfoDaily could not confirm which label, if any, released the album. Our search found no press coverage of the album.

Where to listen and follow

Stream Beers and Ballads on Spotify.

item.title: Burgin, Kentucky's Dillon Carmichael Reunites With Dave Cobb on 'High Ground,' and Here's Why That Matters
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Burgin, Kentucky country singer Dillon Carmichael releases 'High Ground' on Riser House, co-produced by Dave Cobb, who made his 2018 debut.
item.content:encoded:
The Riser House singer and nephew of John Michael and Eddie Montgomery returns to the producer behind his 2018 debut.

Burgin, Kentucky country singer Dillon Carmichael released "High Ground" on Sept. 4, 2026, and the credits carry a familiar name. Dave Cobb, who produced Carmichael's 2018 debut album Hell on an Angel, co-produced the new single with Aaron Raitiere, according to the track's official YouTube listing.

The song runs 3:07, and the listing carries a 2026 Riser House Records phonogram line, the label Carmichael signed with in 2017. Nashville blog That Nashville Sound shared a music video for it on Sept. 5.

Country runs in the family

Carmichael grew up in Burgin and is the nephew of country singers John Michael Montgomery and Eddie Montgomery, a member of Montgomery Gentry. Country Central reports he began performing as a teenager, honing his craft in local bars and talent competitions, before heading to Nashville to pursue a music career.

Critics have taken notice. The Grand Ole Opry's artist page quotes The New York Times saying his baritone on Hell on an Angel "moves with the heft and certainty of a tractor-trailer," and Parade declaring, "Carmichael defines pure country."

From Hell on an Angel to Keepin' Country Alive

After the Cobb-produced debut, Carmichael released Son of A in 2021, co-produced by Jon Pardi, and Keepin' Country Alive, his third studio album, on June 13, 2025. That 14-track set included "Raised Up Wrong," "No Matter How Hard I Try," "Tiny Little Fiddle" and "I'd Call Grandpa."

At radio, "Son of A" and "Drinkin' Problems" each peaked at No. 31 on Country Airplay, per Wikipedia. The Opry page notes the Country Radio Seminar named him a "New Faces" honoree for 2024 and that he was set to join Jon Pardi, Cody Johnson and Luke Bryan on tour that year, on top of headline dates across the U.S. and Europe. The Opry also points to Where I Grew Up, a four-track project that highlights his bluegrass roots.

Why the Cobb credit matters

Cobb produced the album that introduced Carmichael, the record that drew that New York Times line. Eight years after Hell on an Angel, his name is back in the producer credits of a Carmichael single.

"High Ground" is one of several 2026 singles. Apple Music also lists "Huckleberry" and his latest release, "Honky Tonk in Heaven," out Oct. 16, 2026. The Opry credits him with tour dates alongside Dwight Yoakam, and Country Central says he has shared the stage with Luke Bryan and Cody Johnson.

Where to listen and follow

item.title: Clovis, California's Josh Hokit Drops Ciryl Gane Diss Track 'MSG Freestyle' Ahead of UFC 334
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: UFC heavyweight Josh Hokit drops 'MSG Freestyle' as J-Word, a diss track aimed at Ciryl Gane before their UFC 334 title fight at Madison Square Garden.
item.content:encoded:
Rapping as J-Word, the undefeated heavyweight fired his first shots on wax 12 days before his title fight at Madison Square Garden.

Clovis, California's Josh Hokit is taking the trash talk to the booth. Twelve days before he challenges Ciryl Gane for the UFC heavyweight title, the undefeated contender released "MSG Freestyle," a music video he's billing as his first song, under the rap name J-Word.

The roughly two-and-a-half-minute track landed on Hokit's YouTube channel over the weekend, and the main target is no mystery. Gane gets called out from the opening ad-libs, but "The Incredible Hok" spreads the smoke around, with shots at Jon Jones, Alex Pereira and Ilia Topuria, plus a crude line about former First Lady Michelle Obama that's already drawing attention.

The Fight Behind the Freestyle

The song's title is a nod to the venue. Hokit (10-0) meets Gane (14-2, 1 NC) in the main event of UFC 334 on Saturday, Nov. 14, at Madison Square Garden in New York City, streaming on Paramount+. It's Gane's first defense as undisputed heavyweight champion and Hokit's first career main event. Kayla Harrison vs. Amanda Nunes for the bantamweight title is the co-main.

Both men got here by way of the UFC's White House card in June. Gane stopped Alex Pereira to claim the interim belt, then was elevated to undisputed champion after Tom Aspinall vacated. Hokit, a late addition to that card, stopped Derrick Lewis by second-round TKO.

From Fresno State to the Booth

Before MMA, Hokit was a two-sport star at Fresno State, an All-American wrestler who also ran the ball for the Bulldogs, and he later spent time with the San Francisco 49ers. Now he's adding rapper to the résumé, and fans seem into it: the comment section under the video is packed with requests for Hokit to use the track as his walkout song at MSG.

Even Gane's camp admits the challenger can sell a fight. Head coach Fernand Lopez has praised Hokit's pressure and output while acknowledging he knows exactly how to build hype.

Whether J-Word has a second single in him may depend on what happens Nov. 14. Either way, he has the whole heavyweight division listening.

item.title: This Brooklyn, New York Rapper Turned “She Bugging” Into a Meme: Khantrast
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Khantrast is Anthony Zhang, a Brooklyn, New York rapper. The story behind the “She Bugging” official music video, the meme and his other songs.
item.content:encoded:
Anthony Zhang went from anime freestyles to New York drill. Here’s the story behind “She Bugging” and the “Baby You Buggin’” trend.

Khantrast is Anthony Zhang, a Chinese American rapper from Brooklyn, New York, and the voice behind “She Bugging (Whatchu Gonna Do),” the 2026 single whose official music video turned into a TikTok meme. Born in 1998 to Chinese immigrant parents, he went from anime freestyles to New York drill, and he has stayed independent the whole way.

Where is Khantrast from?

Brooklyn. Zhang is fluent in Mandarin and slips it into his music; KQED notes that “Valedictorian” features a verse rapped entirely in the language. He started posting songs to SoundCloud in 2017 and built an early following on anime-themed freestyles, with nods to Naruto, Demon Slayer and Jujutsu Kaisen. In 2022 he broke through with viral songs including “She Bad” and “Let’s Ride,” and dropped the Oppsmas EP.

“Landed in Brooklyn” and the breakout

The real turning point was “Landed in Brooklyn” in 2024, which pushed his sound toward New York drill. KQED reports the July video made him an internet sensation and earned him an On the Radar appearance, and a 2025 remix added Kyle Richh. The song also sparked debate over its use of Asian stereotypes, from lyrics to the straw rice-paddy hat in his videos. Rapper Dumbfoundead criticized the wider trend, while KQED wrote that Khantrast’s imagery comes from a place of pride. In April 2025 he kicked off his first tour, a four-city run that opened at San Francisco’s Brick and Mortar Music Hall.

What is “She Bugging” about?

Produced by Flint, “She Bugging” is a laid-back, loop-driven track that flips the gold-digger story: the woman he is chasing has her own money and pays for dinner. LiFTED Asia points out that the opening line plays on the idea of “yellow fever,” slang for a fetish for Asian partners. The official music video dropped June 5, 2026. Shot by Paul Song in Brooklyn at night, it moves through a claw-machine arcade, a nail salon and a gold-buying shop, a setting LiFTED called New York and Asian at the same time. Khantrast wears a Project X Paris Revolt zip jacket throughout, and the brand reported more than 100,000 views in the first seven days.

How “She Bugging” became the “Baby You Buggin’” meme

On September 30, 2026, Genius posted a Verified video of Khantrast breaking down the song. TikTok users started clipping his sung explanation of the hook that same day, and Know Your Meme now tracks the trend as “Baby You Buggin’.” One early edit passed 1.2 million views in six days, and a reenactment topped one million in two. Most versions use the clip whenever someone is bugging, meaning acting crazy.

Khantrast’s latest music

The meme landed in a busy year. In 2026 Khantrast released the Fake Love EP and tracks including “Malfunction,” “Lovesick” and an “ADD” remix, after opening the year with “Grimey Freestyle.”

Khantrast on YourInfoDaily

For the full rundown on the video, the producer credit and the viral moment, read Khantrast drops new music video for “She Bugging”. For a grittier look at his range from earlier in the year, see our January post, Khantrast shares music video for “Grimey Freestyle”.

Quick answers

What is Khantrast’s real name? Anthony Zhang.

Where is Khantrast from? Brooklyn, New York, where he was born to Chinese immigrant parents.

Who produced “She Bugging”? Flint. The official music video, shot by Paul Song, came out June 5, 2026.

What is the “Baby You Buggin’” meme? A TikTok trend built on Khantrast’s Genius Verified breakdown of “She Bugging.”

item.title: From “Mari Glock” to a Jail-Cell Ballad: Chicago, Illinois’ Lil Noonie
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Lil Noonie is a Chicago, Illinois drill rapper behind “Mari Glock” with Lil Sy. His real name, where he’s from, Lil Sy and his other songs.
item.content:encoded:
The Chicago drill rapper behind the Lil Sy collab “Mari Glock,” what’s known about his name, and the songs that came next.

Lil Noonie is a drill rapper from Chicago, Illinois, best known for “Mari Glock,” his 2025 single with fellow rapper Lil Sy. The two-minute track dropped September 16, 2025, came with an official music video and later anchored his debut album. As for his real name, no credible outlet has published it, and his releases credit him simply as Lil Noonie.

Where is Lil Noonie from?

Chicago. It’s Hip Hop Music calls him a rising Chicago talent bubbling out of the Midwest, and his catalog wears the city on its sleeve, including a guest spot on Glockboy Stank’s “Chiraq.” Hot 97 and The Source both describe his foundation as aggressive drill. His age, neighborhood and legal name have not been reported by any reliable source.

What is “Mari Glock” by Lil Noonie and Lil Sy?

“Mari Glock” is a drill single credited to Lil Noonie and Lil Sy, released under a Lil Noonie / Create Music Group credit. Jeremiah Bolden produced it, and Shazam lists Bolden and Lil Sy as its writers. It’s Hip Hop Music praised Noonie’s hyper-focused cadence and said the official video plays less like a staged shoot and more like a victory lap for their circle.

The song resurfaced on 51 Days & 54 Nights Walkin, a 13-track, 30-minute album released December 12, 2025, through Born With Motion and Create Music Group. It sits alongside “Choppa Season,” “Shark Business” and the closer, “Noonie Home.”

Who is Lil Sy?

Lil Sy is the featured voice on “Mari Glock,” taking the second verse. It’s Hip Hop Music singled out his calculated lyricism as the counterweight to Noonie’s relentless delivery. His streaming catalog is compact: three 2025 singles, “Mari Glock,” “FTO” and “Walk Da Bity,” the last released November 14, 2025. No reliable outlet has reported his hometown, age or real name, so treat claims floating around online with caution.

Lil Noonie’s other songs

Noonie moves fast. Beyond “Mari Glock,” his most-played tracks on Apple Music include “Choppa Season,” “Shark Business,” “Ready or Not,” “End Your Service,” “Anxiety,” “Warzone” and “In Action.” He also turns up as a guest on Glockboy Stank’s “Chiraq,” Cobo75’s “Don’t Think Twice” and Fullydrac’s “DRACBOYZ.”

In 2026 he followed up with a second album, Our Side of the Story, plus a steady stream of singles: “Many Men,” “Wanna Be Opps,” “No Discussion” and “Not Me,” which arrived October 9.

“Searching Through Phones” and a softer side

The biggest left turn is “Searching Through Phones,” a melodic, reflective record. Hot 97 and The Source both report that he wrote it while locked up and grieving the loss of his older brother, freestyling with no beat at all. He has named Polo G as an inspiration, with Hot 97 adding THF. He admits he did not like the song at first, but it grew on him, and fans have pushed him to keep exploring that lane. The message, in his framing, is simple: keep pushing through the pain.

Lil Noonie on YourInfoDaily

We covered the visual in Lil Noonie and Lil Sy drop music video for “Mari Glock”, which breaks down the single, Lil Sy’s second verse and where the track landed on 51 Days & 54 Nights Walkin. Check back here as new music arrives.

Quick answers

What is Lil Noonie’s real name? It has not been made public. His official releases credit him only as Lil Noonie.

Where is Lil Noonie from? Chicago, Illinois, where he came up in the city’s drill scene.

Who is on “Mari Glock” with Lil Noonie? Lil Sy, who raps the second verse and shares a writing credit.

What album is “Mari Glock” on? 51 Days & 54 Nights Walkin, released December 12, 2025.

item.title: Comethazine’s New Name: East St. Louis, Illinois Rapper Is Now Frank Kole
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Comethazine’s new name is Frank Kole (not Frank Cole). The East St. Louis, Illinois “Walk” rapper now makes rock and jazz. Here is what he’s released.
item.content:encoded:
The “Walk” rapper traded trap for guitars and trumpet. Here is when the switch happened and what he’s released since.

Comethazine’s new name is Frank Kole. The East St. Louis, Illinois rapper born Frank Childress, who blew up in 2018 with the viral hit “Walk,” dropped the Comethazine name after his Bawskee run and now makes alternative rock and jazz-leaning music as Frank Kole. That is Kole with a K, even though plenty of fans search it as Frank Cole.

Where is Comethazine from?

Childress was born July 6, 1998, and came up in East St. Louis, Illinois. His SoundCloud breakthrough came with “Hella Choppers” in October 2017, and “Might Cop,” posted on the Eleven YouTube page, got music executives paying attention. He went on to release his projects through Alamo Records and later launched his own imprint, Hench Mafia Records, in 2019.

Comethazine’s breakout songs

“Walk” is the one everybody remembers. The 2018 single came with a Cole Bennett-directed Lyrical Lemonade video, climbed to No. 20 on the Billboard Bubbling Under Hot 100, went platinum and also exists in a version with A$AP Rocky. “Bands” went gold after an early 2018 SoundCloud glitch swapped it in for YBN Nahmir’s “Bounce Out with That,” sending a wave of new ears his way. Both landed on his debut mixtape Bawskee in August 2018. From there came Bawskee 2, Bawskee 3.5, the album Pandemic in March 2020, Bawskee 4, Comethazine the Album in October 2021 and Bawskee 5 in November 2022.

When did Comethazine change his name to Frank Kole?

After Bawskee 5, he went quiet. In March 2024, HotNewHipHop reported he had resurfaced on Instagram after a two-year break, rocking a mustache and a ’70s rock-star look and showing off guitar work. The Frank Kole name followed with his first single under it, “Smokestack Lightning,” in October 2024. He has not publicly explained why he made the switch, and no outlet we checked has a reason on record.

What has Frank Kole released?

“Smokestack Lightning” is still the only Frank Kole song on streaming platforms, according to Elicit Magazine in February 2026. Most of the new era lives on YouTube, under the channel Franzkole. There he plays several instruments, including trumpet on a jazz take of Joseph Kosma’s standard “Autumn Leaves” with a pianist. We covered that clip when it landed in November 2025: Frank Kole, formerly known as Comethazine, drops music video for “Autumn Leaves”. In January 2026 he followed it with a visualizer for “Feels of Rhien.”

Quick answers

What is Comethazine’s new name? Frank Kole, spelled with a K.

Is Frank Kole the same person as Comethazine? Yes. Both names belong to Frank Childress of East St. Louis, Illinois.

Why did Comethazine change his name? He has not said publicly. The name change came with a full switch from rap to rock and jazz.

What is Comethazine’s most famous song? “Walk,” the platinum 2018 single from Bawskee.

item.title: Shoreline Mafia Members: How the Los Angeles, California Crew Went From 4 to 2
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Who’s in Shoreline Mafia? The Los Angeles, California group began with OhGeesy, Fenix Flexin, Rob Vicious and Master Kato. Today it’s a duo. Full lineup history.
item.content:encoded:
OhGeesy, Fenix Flexin, Rob Vicious and Master Kato: the lineup, the 2020 split, the reunion and the hit “Bands.”

Shoreline Mafia started as a four-man rap crew from Los Angeles, California: OhGeesy (Alejandro Carranza), Fenix Flexin (Fenix Rypinski), Rob Vicious (Robert Magee) and Master Kato (Malik Carson). Today the group is a duo of OhGeesy and Fenix Flexin, who reunited after a 2020 split and have been dropping new Shoreline music since 2024.

Who is in Shoreline Mafia?

OhGeesy and Fenix Flexin are the core. The two met in 2012 doing graffiti around Los Angeles and started making music soon after. Shoreline became a proper rap group in 2016, when they brought in Rob Vicious and Master Kato. Fenix was born in San Diego and bounced through Oceanside, Chula Vista, Huntington Park and Downey before landing in East Hollywood. Rob Vicious hails from LA’s West Adams, while HotNewHipHop notes Master Kato was born and raised in Chicago, making him the only member not from California.

Shoreline Mafia lineup changes, year by year

2016: The four-man lineup forms and drops the independent EP Trapped It Out that December.

2018: Atlantic signs the group in May and re-releases the 2017 breakout tape ShoreLineDoThatShit.

April 2020: Fenix Flexin announces he is leaving to chase his own creative vision, calling the split amicable. The rest of the crew soon goes solo too, and the quartet’s run ends with the July 2020 debut album Mafia Bidness, which hit No. 27 on the Billboard 200. Rob Vicious and Master Kato’s time in the group closes out that year.

2024 to now: OhGeesy and Fenix Flexin bring the name back as a duo. The single “Heat Stick” became their first Billboard Hot 100 entry, they performed at Kendrick Lamar’s Pop Out concert in June 2024, and the comeback album Back in Bidness landed April 4, 2025, ahead of their Coachella set. The eight-track EP Bidness Is Boomin followed on May 1, 2026.

Shoreline Mafia’s biggest songs

The street-party anthems “Musty” and “Nun Major” from ShoreLineDoThatShit both went platinum, and “Musty” put producer Ron-Ron in the group’s orbit. The biggest of all is “Bands,” the 2018 cut from Rob Vicious’ Traplantic tape, now certified double platinum. Later hits include “Gangstas & Sippas” with Q Da Fool and YG, and “Hollywood” with YG in 2025.

Shoreline Mafia on YourInfoDaily

We were there for the first run. Start with the “Bands” video, back when all four members were in the frame. OhGeesy linked with Detroit’s BandGang for “Homicide” featuring BandGang Lonnie Bands, a Ron-Ron production from the holiday tape OTXmas. That same project gave us the “Molly Water” video. The crew also teamed with Watts native 03 Greedo on “Traphouse,” a video where Greedo appears only as a cardboard cutout.

What are the former members doing now?

Rob Vicious stayed busy solo with his Fearless mixtape series, which reached Fearless 5 in November 2024, plus the June 2025 EP Kuma Vicious with King Kuma. OhGeesy and Fenix both built solo catalogs during the break, and Fenix dropped Fenix Flexin Vol. 1 in 2021.

Quick answers

Who are the Shoreline Mafia members? Currently OhGeesy and Fenix Flexin. Rob Vicious and Master Kato were members from 2016 to 2020.

Who’s in Shoreline Mafia today? Just the duo of OhGeesy and Fenix Flexin, back together since 2024.

What is Shoreline Mafia’s “Bands”? A 2018 single from Rob Vicious’ Traplantic mixtape, certified 2× Platinum by the RIAA.

Where is Shoreline Mafia from? Los Angeles, California.

item.title: How Atlanta, Georgia’s Belly Gang Kushington Landed 21 Savage on “WTF Goin”
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Belly Gang Kushington’s “WTF Goin” with 21 Savage dropped June 19, 2026. How the Atlanta, Georgia rapper landed the feature and what came next.
item.content:encoded:
A snippet, a reach-out from London and a Magic City wings order: the Adamsville rapper’s breakout year, explained.

“WTF Goin” is the June 19, 2026 single from Belly Gang Kushington, the rapper from Atlanta, Georgia, and it features 21 Savage. The Magic City-shouting anthem gave Belly his first Billboard Hot 100 entry, has passed 100 million streams worldwide and comes with an official video that opens with the two rappers landing a helicopter at the club.

What is “WTF Goin” with 21 Savage?

It started as a short snippet Belly posted online. 21 Savage heard it while he was in London, reached out directly and cut his verse once he got home, with no label managers or middlemen involved, according to Belly. Belly co-produced the horn-heavy beat with Musik MajorX, Kutta Beatz, B100 and Squat Beats. The hook is a challenge: who actually has the money and respect to matter? The verses run through Atlanta roots, past hustling and plans to buy back a property he once rented, and 21 delivers one of his sharper guest spots in a while. A TikTok dance trend carried it beyond Atlanta, and Complex reports it peaked at No. 43 on the Hot 100. There is also an alternate “Magic City Edition” cut of the video.

Who is Belly Gang Kushington?

Belly Gang Kushington is Victor Thomas, raised by his father in the Adamsville neighborhood of Atlanta, Georgia. He started rapping in 2020, dropped a string of local singles like “5pm in Atlanta,” and signed with Love Renaissance (LVRN) in late 2024. His debut album, The Streets Is Yours, arrived April 25, 2025. The breakout was the “Friend Do” remix with YKNiece, which hit No. 20 on Billboard’s Hot Rap Songs and became a fixture in Atlanta clubs by the end of 2025.

Belly Gang Kushington’s breakout year

2026 has been stacked. Billboard named him Hip-Hop Rookie of the Month in March, he earned a BET Award nomination for Best New Artist in May, and he landed on the 2026 XXL Freshman list in June. In September, he and BigXthaPlug announced a joint single, “LITE.” Then the wings came full circle: Magic City Kitchen permanently renamed its 10-piece lemon pepper wings meal “Belly Gang,” a nod to the “WTF Goin” lyric that already had TikTok arguing over who serves Atlanta’s best wings.

Get the full rundown on the 21 Savage link-up in our “WTF Goin” breakdown, which covers how Belly went from Adamsville to the BET Awards conversation. If you want the debut album era, start with our guide to “Call Back Kush”, a cut from The Streets Is Yours.

Quick answers

Who is on “WTF Goin”? Belly Gang Kushington featuring 21 Savage.

When did “WTF Goin” come out? June 19, 2026, as a standalone single. No parent album has been announced.

Where is Belly Gang Kushington from? Adamsville, Atlanta, Georgia.

What is the Magic City “Belly Gang” order? A 10-piece lemon pepper wings meal at Magic City Kitchen, renamed after the “WTF Goin” lyric.

item.title: Pompano Beach, Florida’s Loe Shimmy Shoots His Shot on “Seduce You”
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Loe Shimmy’s “Seduce You” is a melodic love song from Pretty Girlz Run The World. Meet the Pompano Beach, Florida rapper and his biggest hits.
item.content:encoded:
The Florida hitmaker behind “For Me,” “3am” and “I’m Spent” gets romantic on Pretty Girlz Run The World.

“Seduce You” is a melodic love song from Loe Shimmy, the rapper from Pompano Beach, Florida, and it sits at track six on his album Pretty Girlz Run The World, released July 24, 2026, through Rebel and gamma. Shimmy sings more than he raps on it, and the official video gives the song a glossy, stylish finish that matches its flirty mood.

What is Loe Shimmy’s “Seduce You”?

Think of it as Shimmy shooting his shot in full falsetto. The record blends his street rap roots with smooth, dance-ready pop production, and the chorus is the part that sticks. It landed as part of a 21-track album built around romance, nightlife and late-night feelings, so “Seduce You” is right on theme. The official video arrived in the days after the album dropped.

Where is Loe Shimmy from?

Loe Shimmy is Shamar Williams Cox, born March 24, 1999, in Pompano Beach, Florida. He debuted in 2020 with Zombie Land, mixing gritty street raps with melodic songs about love and nightlife, delivered in a high-pitched, nasal voice that he admits confused listeners at first. Drake reposted his song “Tina” in 2022, and the two later connected in the studio. That same year, The FADER was already spotlighting tracks like “Not The Same” and “On The Run.”

Loe Shimmy’s biggest songs

The breakout was “For Me” in 2024, which debuted at No. 78 on the Billboard Hot 100 and went gold, with a Brent Faiyaz remix that went gold too. “3am” with Don Toliver followed in 2025, peaking at No. 71 and also going gold, off Rockstar Junkie, a 37-song album that dropped July 18, 2025. His biggest hit so far is “I’m Spent” with Drake, from Habibti, which reached No. 34 on the Hot 100. Along the way he joined XXL’s Freshman class, opened for Lil Baby on the WHAM Tour and crossed roughly 2 billion global streams.

What is on Pretty Girlz Run The World?

The new album trims things down to 21 tracks and debuted at No. 68 on the Billboard 200. Brent Faiyaz returns on “Run The World,” Summer Walker shows up on “Just Saying” and Sexyy Red brings the chaos on “5 Star Freak.” “Body Dangerous” and “Bag Rite” were the singles, while the D3-produced “Aruba” is the summer sleeper. Elsewhere, “Everyday” samples Cherrelle’s “Saturday Love” and “I Bleed Too” is the most personal moment on the record.

Loe Shimmy on YourInfoDaily

We broke down the song and its visual in our “Seduce You” video story, including what the track is about and how the album performed. Before that, Shimmy went worldwide in the globe-trotting “Bag Rite” video, directed by Juan Galarza. Go back to the Zombieland 2 era of 2024 for “Zuper,” his music video with Wizz Havinn.

Quick answers

What album is “Seduce You” by Loe Shimmy on? Pretty Girlz Run The World, released July 24, 2026. It is track six.

Does “Seduce You” have a music video? Yes. Loe Shimmy released an official video for the song shortly after the album came out.

Where is Loe Shimmy from? Pompano Beach, Florida.

What is Loe Shimmy’s biggest song? “I’m Spent” with Drake, which peaked at No. 34 on the Billboard Hot 100.

item.title: Alaska Atmos Points Sale: Buy Now or Wait?
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Should you buy Alaska Atmos Rewards points in the current sale or wait for the next one? A simple decision guide with real prices and sale history.
item.content:encoded:
With bonuses returning every couple of months, the question is not whether a sale is good. It is whether you have a seat to book.

Disclosure: YourInfoDaily may earn a commission if you buy through links in this article. Offers change and are often targeted, so confirm the terms in your own account before buying.

Buy now if you have found an award seat you want and the points cost less than the cash fare. Wait if you are buying for a trip that does not exist yet. Alaska puts Atmos Rewards points on sale often enough that missing one costs you very little.

Here is how to decide in about five minutes.

What the latest sale looks like

One Mile at a Time reported a bonus of up to 100% on purchased Atmos Rewards points running October 2 to October 19, 2026. In the author's account, the tiers were:

  • 5,000 to 14,000 points: 80% bonus
  • 15,000 to 29,000 points: 90% bonus
  • 30,000 to 100,000 points: 100% bonus

At the top tier, buying 100,000 points costs $3,762.50 and returns 200,000 points, or about 1.88 cents per point. The standard price is 3.5 cents per point before tax.

Offers are targeted. Readers reported bonuses ranging from none to 120% depending on the account and country. What your login shows is the only number that counts. If you are reading this after October 19, check whether a new offer has replaced it.

How often do Atmos points go on sale?

Often. The sale before this one ran July 30 to August 20, 2026, which left a gap of about six weeks between offers. One Mile at a Time's deal history shows a steady run of promotions.

That pattern is the most useful fact in this article. A sale ending is not a deadline you have to meet. Another is likely on the way, though the bonus size is never guaranteed.

The five-minute decision

Question 1: Do you have a specific flight?

If no, wait. Points you cannot use yet are money parked in a currency someone else controls. If yes, go on.

Question 2: Is the award seat available right now?

Search on Alaska's site for your route and dates. Partner seats are limited to what each airline releases. If you can see the seat today, that matters more than the bonus size. If you cannot, buying will not make it appear.

Question 3: Do points beat cash?

Multiply the points price by your cost per point, add the taxes and fees, and compare with the cash fare.

  • Example: a 75,000-point business class award at 1.88 cents costs about $1,410 in points. Upgraded Points reported that price in February 2026 for Japan Airlines from Tokyo to Chicago. If the cash fare is $4,000, that is an easy yes.
  • Counter-example: a 12,500-point domestic flight costs about $235 in bought points. If the cash fare is $180, pay cash.

Question 4: Can you reach the top tier?

The best bonus applies to purchases of 30,000 points or more. If you need 28,000, compare the cost of buying 30,000 at the higher tier. Sometimes buying slightly more costs about the same per trip and leaves you a small balance.

[Alaska Atmos Rewards Points - Check the Atmos Rewards bonus on your account]

Three reasons to buy now

  • The seat is there. Premium cabin award space on partners comes and goes. An available seat is the scarce thing, not the sale.
  • You can cancel. Katie's Travel Tricks reports that Atmos awards have no change or cancellation fees, with points returned and taxes refunded. A partner booking fee, reported at $20 per direction, is not refunded. Booking early carries little risk.
  • Your offer is at the top of the range. A 100% bonus is the level most enthusiasts wait for.

Three reasons to wait

  • No trip. One Mile at a Time values an Atmos point at about 1.5 cents. At 1.88 cents, you are paying above that, so you need a strong redemption to come out ahead.
  • A weak offer. If your account shows 40% or 50%, your cost per point is far higher. Sit this one out.
  • A new account. Your Atmos account must be at least 10 days old to buy points. If you just joined, the next sale is your sale.

The limits

  • Non-elite members can buy up to 150,000 points per calendar year, not counting bonus points. Elite members have no limit.
  • Each transaction is capped at 100,000 points before bonuses, and you can make multiple transactions.
  • Points.com processes the purchase, so it does not count as airfare on a credit card.
  • Points do not expire as long as the account has activity every 24 months.

What if you wait and the seat disappears?

That is the real risk of waiting, and it is why the order of operations matters. If you have a seat in view and the math works, buy and book. If you are only watching the sale and not a seat, you are not losing anything by letting it pass.

One specific warning: One Mile at a Time reports that American is pulling saver award space from partner programs within six days of departure. Don't plan last-minute American seats with Atmos points.

The verdict

Seat first, sale second. A good sale with no seat is a bad purchase. A seat you want during any decent bonus is a good one.

[Alaska Atmos Rewards Points - See your current Atmos Rewards price per point]

FAQ

What is a good price for Atmos points?

Around 1.88 cents per point, the cost at a 100% bonus, is the benchmark enthusiasts watch for.

When is the next Alaska points sale?

Alaska does not announce a schedule. Recent sales were about six weeks apart.

How soon can a new member buy points?

The account must be at least 10 days old.

Can I buy more than 100,000 points?

Yes, across multiple transactions, up to 150,000 a year for non-elite members before bonus points.

item.title: Why Points Nerds Keep Buying Alaska Atmos Points

item.description: Why do frequent flyers keep buying Alaska Atmos Rewards points? Partner airlines, free stopovers, and no change fees. See the costs and the catches.
item.content:encoded:
It is not about flying Alaska. It is about who Alaska's points can put you on.

Disclosure: YourInfoDaily may earn a commission if you buy through links in this article. Offers change and are often targeted, so confirm the terms in your own account before buying.

Points enthusiasts keep buying Alaska Atmos Rewards points because they open seats on more than two dozen partner airlines, allow a free stopover, and can be canceled without a fee. People buy them to fly Japan Airlines, Qatar Airways, or Starlux, often in business class, for less than the cash fare.

That is the appeal. There are real catches too, and both are below.

What is Atmos Rewards?

Atmos Rewards is Alaska Airlines' loyalty program, formerly known as Mileage Plan, and it now covers Hawaiian Airlines as well. You do not have to live on the West Coast or fly Alaska to use it. Many members never do.

Reason 1: The partner list

One Mile at a Time lists the airlines you can book with Atmos points. They include American, British Airways, Cathay Pacific, Japan Airlines, Qantas, Qatar Airways, Finnair, Iberia, Aer Lingus, Korean Air, Fiji Airways, Air Tahiti Nui, Condor, Icelandair, Starlux, Hawaiian, Royal Air Maroc, and more.

For a touring artist or a founder with meetings abroad, that balance reaches Asia, Europe, the Middle East, the South Pacific, and most of the United States.

Reason 2: Business class at a known price

Published examples show why people do the math. Upgraded Points reported these one-way business class awards in February 2026, plus taxes and fees:

  • Japan Airlines, Tokyo to Chicago: 75,000 points.
  • Starlux Airlines, Phoenix to Taipei: 85,000 points.

During the most recent sale, One Mile at a Time put the best price at 1.88 cents per point. At that rate, 75,000 points cost about $1,410 and 85,000 cost about $1,598. Long-haul business class fares commonly run several times that. Award prices can change, so confirm current rates before you buy.

Reason 3: A free stopover

Atmos allows a stopover on partner awards at no extra points cost, even on a one-way ticket, according to One Mile at a Time. You can break a trip in a partner's hub city for days and continue on the same award. The exception is awards entirely within Asia.

For anyone combining a show, a meeting, and a few days off, that is two destinations for the price of one.

Reason 4: Low fees and no penalty for changing plans

Most partners do not add fuel surcharges to Atmos awards. One Mile at a Time names British Airways, Hainan, and Icelandair as exceptions.

Katie's Travel Tricks reports that Atmos award flights carry no change or cancellation fees, with points returned to your account and taxes refunded. The one cost that doesn't come back is a partner award booking fee, which the site lists at $20 per direction.

That flexibility helps buyers feel comfortable booking early. If a tour date moves, the points come home.

[Alaska Atmos Rewards Points - Check your Alaska Atmos Rewards points offer]

Reason 5: Sales come around often

The standard price is steep at 3.5 cents per point before tax. One Mile at a Time notes it used to be 2.75 cents. Almost nobody pays that. The program runs frequent bonuses:

  • July 30 to August 20, 2026: a bonus sale.
  • October 2 to October 19, 2026: a bonus of up to 100%, with reported tiers of 80% for 5,000 to 14,000 points, 90% for 15,000 to 29,000, and 100% for 30,000 to 100,000.

Offers are targeted. Some members reported seeing higher or lower bonuses than the published tiers, and some outside the United States reported none. Log in to see what your account shows.

Reason 6: Short flights are cheap too

It is not all first-class suites. Katie's Travel Tricks lists U.S. domestic awards from 4,500 points each way, and One Mile at a Time describes Atmos as good value for short and medium flights, especially on American. For a quick hop between tour stops, a small balance goes a long way.

The catches

  • The price is above the valuation. One Mile at a Time values an Atmos point at about 1.5 cents. Buying at 1.88 cents only makes sense for a redemption that beats that, which usually means premium cabins or expensive last-minute fares.
  • Partner seats are limited. You can only book what partners release. One Mile at a Time reports that American is pulling saver award space from partner programs within six days of departure.
  • There are limits. Non-elite members can buy up to 150,000 points per calendar year, not counting bonus points, with a maximum of 100,000 per transaction. The account must be at least 10 days old.
  • It is not airfare to your card. Points.com processes the sale, so it does not count as an airline purchase.
  • Programs change. Award charts can be revised. Buy for a trip you can book now.

How to buy like the people who do this well

  • Find the award seat first on Alaska's site.
  • Check the points price and the taxes.
  • Compare with the cash fare for the same flight.
  • Buy during a bonus, in an amount that hits the top tier if you need that many points.
  • Book as soon as the points arrive.

[Alaska Atmos Rewards Points - See your Atmos Rewards bonus and price out your award]

FAQ

Do I need to fly Alaska Airlines to use Atmos points?

No. Points can be redeemed on partner airlines around the world.

How much do Atmos points cost?

The standard price is 3.5 cents each before tax. With a 100% bonus, the cost is about 1.88 cents.

Do Atmos points expire?

Not as long as the account has activity at least once every 24 months.

Can I cancel an Atmos award ticket?

Yes. Reports indicate no change or cancellation fee, though a partner booking fee is not refunded.

item.title: 5 Mistakes People Make Buying Hilton Honors Points
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Buying Hilton Honors points? Avoid five common mistakes, from trusting the headline bonus to booking the wrong room type, and keep the savings.
item.content:encoded:
The sale price is only half the story. These five errors turn a good deal into an expensive one.

Disclosure: YourInfoDaily may earn a commission if you buy through links in this article. Offers change and are often targeted, so confirm the terms in your own account before buying.

The five mistakes are trusting the headline bonus, booking the wrong room, ignoring the fifth night, paying with the wrong expectations about your card, and buying more points than you need. Each one is easy to avoid once you know it exists.

The context: One Mile at a Time reports a Hilton Honors bonus of up to 120% on purchased points from October 7 to November 21, 2026, which brings the cost as low as about 0.45 cents per point.

Mistake 1: Trusting the headline bonus

The phrase to notice is up to. Hilton's purchase bonuses are targeted, and different members may see different offers. A friend's 120% can be your 100% or less.

There is also a floor. The current bonus applies to purchases of at least 5,000 points in a single transaction. Buy fewer and you pay the standard one cent per point.

The fix: log in and read the offer attached to your own account. Do the math with your number, not the one in the headline.

Mistake 2: Pricing the wrong room

Hilton has no published award chart. The points price depends on the hotel, the date, and the room type. One Mile at a Time puts standard free nights at roughly 10,000 to 250,000 points, with premium rooms priced higher.

People often see a low points price in a search, buy points, and then find that the standard rooms are gone and only premium rooms remain at a much higher rate. The Points Guy notes that the price cap applies to a property's standard rate, not to every room.

The fix: search your exact dates and confirm that a standard room reward is available before you buy. Then book promptly once the points arrive.'

Mistake 3: Ignoring the fifth night

Members with Silver status or higher get the fifth night free on standard room reward stays, according to The Points Guy. The benefit applies to stays of up to 20 nights.

This cuts two ways:

  • If you have status and need five nights, you only need points for four. Buying five nights' worth wastes money.
  • If you need four nights and have status, check a fifth. An extra night can cost nothing.

Silver comes with some Hilton credit cards, and it is the lowest elite tier. If you don't have status, the fifth night free doesn't apply, so don't budget for it.

The fix: confirm your status in your account, then size the purchase around the nights you actually pay for.

[See the bonus on your Hilton Honors account.]

Mistake 4: Expecting hotel rewards on the purchase

Points purchases are processed by Points.com, not by Hilton. That has one practical effect: the charge does not count as hotel spending on a credit card, so you should not expect a hotel-category bonus on it.

One Mile at a Time suggests using a card with a minimum spending requirement, or one that earns well on everyday purchases.

The fix: pick the card for its general earning rate, and do not count on a hotel multiplier.

Mistake 5: Buying more than the trip needs

A big bonus makes it tempting to buy the maximum. During this promotion, the cap is 240,000 points before the bonus, up from the usual 160,000 per calendar year, and the top tier turns $2,400 into 528,000 points.

That is a lot of money parked in a currency Hilton controls. With no award chart, the company can raise what a night costs at any time. Points also earn nothing while they wait.

The value benchmarks are worth keeping in view. The Points Guy values a Hilton point at 0.4 cents and One Mile at a Time at 0.5 cents. At 0.45 cents, you are buying at about average value, which only pays off if your redemption is better than average.

The fix: buy what a specific booking requires, plus a small margin. Treat every purchase as final and check the refund terms before you pay.

A bonus mistake: spending points on the wrong things

Hilton lets you use points for rides, shopping, car rentals, and event credits. The Points Guy values those at around 0.2 cents per point. Airline transfers can be as poor as 10,000 points for 1,000 miles. If you paid 0.45 cents, each of those options loses more than half your money.

Hotel nights are where the value is. Keep buying points for rooms.

What a clean purchase looks like

  • You have dates and a hotel.
  • You have confirmed a standard room reward is available and noted the points price.
  • You know the cash price, including taxes.
  • You have multiplied the points by your own sale price and the points version is clearly cheaper.
  • You have checked the hotel's cancellation terms. Most Hilton award stays can be canceled free until a couple of days before arrival, but some properties are stricter.
  • You buy only what you need and book as soon as the points land.

Six checks, about ten minutes. That is the difference between a deal and a donation.

[Run the numbers on your own Hilton offer.]

FAQ

What is the minimum Hilton points purchase for the bonus?

The current promotion requires at least 5,000 points in one transaction.

Why is my Hilton bonus lower than advertised?

Offers are targeted by account. The advertised figure is the highest tier, not a guarantee.

Can I get the fifth night free with points I buy?

Yes, if you hold Silver status or higher and book a standard room reward stay of five nights or more.

Do Hilton points expire after I buy them?

Not as long as the account has activity at least once every 24 months. Buying points counts as activity.

item.title: How to Pick Wine for a Launch Party on a Budget
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Planning a launch or release party? Use this bottle math, a three-wine menu, and a sample Wine Express order for 40 guests under $400.
item.content:encoded:
The bottle math, the three-wine rule, and a sample order for 40 guests that clears free shipping.

Disclosure: YourInfoDaily may earn a commission if you buy through links in this article. This content is intended for readers 21 and over.

For a launch party, buy three wines, plan on roughly one glass per guest per hour, and order at least two weeks ahead. That covers an album release, a store opening, or a product launch without a sommelier or a blown budget.

Below is the math, a sample order, and the delivery details that trip up first-time hosts.

How much wine do you need?

A standard 750 ml bottle pours about five glasses. A common planning rule is one drink per guest per hour, with a little extra in the first hour.

  • Guests x hours = glasses. Forty guests for two hours is about 80 glasses.
  • Glasses / 5 = bottles. Eighty glasses is 16 bottles.
  • Add a 15% cushion. That brings you to 18 or 19 bottles.

If you are also serving beer, cocktails, or a strong non-alcoholic option, cut the wine count by a third. Not everyone drinks, and a good zero-proof choice is part of hosting well.

The three-wine rule

Too many choices slow the bar and leave you with half-empty bottles. Three wines cover nearly every guest:

  • One sparkling. It marks the occasion and photographs well.
  • One red. Medium to full body, nothing too tannic.
  • One white. Crisp and cold.

For an evening launch, split the order roughly 40% sparkling, 30% red, and 30% white. Go heavier on white and sparkling in warm weather or for a daytime event.

A sample order for 40 guests

These prices were listed at Wine Express on October 10, 2026. Several were sale prices, so confirm before ordering.

  • Sparkling: 8 bottles of Mionetto Prosecco Brut, Treviso DOC, at $15.75. Total: $126.00.
  • Red: 6 bottles of Fabio Cordella 2020 Il Castellano Primitivo, Salento, at $16.47 each. Total: $98.82.
  • White: 6 bottles from the under-$20 filter. Budget about $17 each, roughly $102.

That is 20 bottles for about $327 before tax, or a little over $8 per guest. At 12 or more bottles to one address, Wine Express ships ground free, so the delivery line should be zero.

Want one showpiece for the toast? A Belle Glos 2022 Pinot Noir magnum was listed at $85.95 and Moët & Chandon Brut Imperial at $52.95. One big bottle on the table does more for the room than upgrading every pour.

[Price out your party order at Wine Express.]

Where the savings come from

  • Free shipping at volume. Orders of $149 or more, or 12 or more bottles, ship ground free to one address.
  • Case discounts. Buy 12 or more bottles to get up to 15% off eligible wines. Sale-priced wines are excluded, so compare both ways.
  • The price filter. The catalog sorts by price band starting under $20. For a crowd, nobody needs a $50 pour.
  • Skipping the venue markup. Venues often charge well above retail per bottle. If yours allows outside alcohol, ask about the corkage fee and do the comparison.

The timeline

Wine Express says in-stock orders generally ship from New York within one to three days and arrive two to 14 business days after ordering, depending on location. Champagne needs three to five days of processing and cannot be expedited. Shipments may also be delayed due to extreme weather.

  • Three weeks out: confirm the venue's alcohol policy and headcount.
  • Two weeks out: place the order.
  • Delivery day: have an adult 21 or older ready to sign and show ID. A studio or office address works best.
  • Day before: chill whites and sparkling overnight.

Do not cut it close. If a box comes back unsigned, the sender pays return shipping and a 20% restocking fee, and your party has no wine.

Check these before you order

  • State rules. Wine Express does not ship to Alabama, Alaska, Arkansas, Delaware, Hawaii, Kentucky, Michigan, Mississippi, North Dakota, South Dakota, Tennessee, Utah, or Puerto Rico.
  • Venue and permit rules. Some venues require their own bartenders, and selling tickets that include alcohol can trigger local permit requirements. Ask first.
  • Service basics. Check IDs, serve food, stock water, and line up rides. A launch should be remembered for the work.

What to do with leftovers

Keep unopened bottles. Store them in a cool, dark spot, and you'll have client gifts or a head start on the next event. Returns are limited to seven days and carry a 20% restocking fee, so plan to keep what you buy.

[Order early and let Wine Express deliver to your venue or studio.]

FAQ

How many bottles of wine do 50 guests need?

For a two-hour event with wine only, plan for about 20 bottles, plus a few spares. Reduce that if you are serving other drinks.

Is Prosecco fine instead of Champagne?

Yes. For a crowd, it is the budget-smart choice, and it ships faster than Champagne at Wine Express.

How far ahead should I order?

Two weeks is a safe margin given the two to 14 business day delivery window.

Can wine be delivered to a venue?

Yes, if the state is served and an adult 21 or older can sign. Confirm with the venue first.

Should I buy better wine for VIP guests?

Buy one or two special bottles for the toast or the green room and keep the main bar simple. Guests remember the moment the big bottle was opened, not the vintage in their second glass.

item.title: Zippy Raises $20 Million to Modernize the Most Overlooked Corner of the American Housing Market
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Zippy raises a $20M Series C from Saluda Grade to expand manufactured housing loans beyond 27 states and launch new products for communities and retailers.
item.content:encoded:
The manufactured-home lender's Series C from Saluda Grade follows more than $600 million in capital commitments secured this year.

Manufactured homes are one of the last truly affordable paths to owning a home in America. Financing them, however, has long been slow, paper-heavy and underserved by mainstream lenders. Zippy has just raised $20 million to change that.

The tech-enabled lender and loan servicer closed a Series C round with Saluda Grade as the sole investor, committing through its growth equity strategy, FinTech Global reported. Beyond capital, Saluda Grade will support Zippy on credit, capital markets, balance sheet management and product development.

A Lender Built for One Kind of Home

Founded in 2021, Zippy focuses exclusively on manufactured housing finance. It works with manufactured housing communities, retailers, dealers and wholesale partners, and has built its own loan origination platform covering digital applications, partner tools, underwriting, standardized paperwork and data infrastructure.

"Manufactured housing is already one of the most compelling affordable homeownership solutions in America, but it needs a financing system that is just as modern and efficient as the homes themselves," co-founder and CEO Ben Halliday said.

The Numbers Behind the Round

Zippy currently operates in 27 states. In 2026 alone, it has secured more than $600 million in capital commitments, the lending capacity that lets it fund loans at scale. The new equity gives the company room to keep growing that balance sheet while investing in technology.

"Zippy has built an impressive platform in one of the most overlooked sectors of housing finance," said John Stepp, head of ventures at Saluda Grade.

Why Manufactured Housing Is Having a Moment

With home prices and mortgage rates squeezing first-time buyers, manufactured homes offer a far lower entry price than site-built houses. Yet buyers often face higher rates and fewer lending options, in part because many manufactured homes are financed as personal property rather than traditional real estate. Lenders that can underwrite these loans efficiently stand to capture a market that big banks have largely ignored.

That gap is the opportunity Zippy is targeting: a vertical, software-driven lender that understands the economics of manufactured home communities and dealers better than generalist mortgage shops.

Saluda Grade's involvement is also strategic. The firm is known for its work in residential credit and capital markets, expertise that matters for a lender whose growth depends on reliably funding and selling loans. A sole-investor round from a specialist backer suggests conviction in Zippy's underwriting, not just its software.

For buyers, the promise is simple: faster approvals, clearer paperwork and fewer dead ends at the dealership or community office. For the industry, a well-capitalized digital lender could add competition to a segment where options have historically been thin.

What Comes Next

Zippy says the funding will help it expand beyond its current 27-state footprint, launch new loan products through community, retail and wholesale channels, and build out its technology and balance sheet capacity.

If it succeeds, Zippy could help make one of America's most affordable housing options easier to finance, and turn a long-neglected corner of lending into a serious fintech category.

item.title: Affinity Labs Raises $2 Million to Turn Influencers Into Software Founders With AI
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: London's Affinity Labs raises $2M pre-seed led by Fuel Ventures to co-found AI-powered software brands with creators, plus a £497K Innovate UK grant.
item.content:encoded:
The London startup co-founds apps with creators like Olivia Bowen, and says its portfolio revenue has been doubling month over month.

Creators have mastered attention. What most of them have not built is a business that runs without them on camera. London startup Affinity Labs wants to fix that by co-founding software companies with creators, and it just raised $2 million to scale the idea.

The pre-seed round was led by Fuel Ventures, with Antler co-investing, Tech.eu reported. Angel investors from Google DeepMind, Meta and Playfair VC joined, along with creator Marcello Ascani and Kyra CEO Devran Amaratunga Karaca. Affinity Labs also secured a £497,787 grant from Innovate UK, part of UK Research and Innovation.

Creators as Co-Founders

The model is simple to explain and hard to execute. Every product Affinity Labs launches is co-founded with a creator who brings an existing, engaged audience. Affinity Labs supplies the technology, product and operations needed to turn that audience into a paying software brand.

"Creators are the most underleveraged founders in the world," CEO Edoardo Ricci said. "Affinity Labs exists to be that infrastructure, we co-found every product with a leading creator."

Ricci runs the company alongside COO Ahmed Eltom and CTO Sunny Panchal.

AI Does the Heavy Lifting

What makes the approach scalable is a proprietary AI-powered development system that automates stages of the product lifecycle, from identifying software ideas and matching them with creator partners to building, operating and growing the products. That automation is what lets a small team run a portfolio rather than a single app.

Early Traction

Affinity Labs has launched four creator-led brands so far. Interior Design Clinic, built with Olivia Bowen, reached No. 34 in the App Store's Lifestyle category. Archives, built with Basel Ghazoghli, has more than 75,000 users and ranks among the top 200 Education apps. According to the company, portfolio revenue has averaged 100% month-over-month growth over the past three months, meaning it has roughly doubled each month.

Why It Matters

The creator economy has largely monetized through brand deals, merch and consumer products like beverages and cosmetics. Software is a different animal: higher margins, recurring revenue and products that can grow even when the creator takes a break. If AI lowers the cost of building apps far enough, a creator's audience may become the most valuable distribution channel a new software company can have.

What's Next

Affinity Labs will use the funding to expand its portfolio, support existing products and grow its product, growth and engineering teams. Part of the capital, including the Innovate UK grant, will go toward its AI product development technology.

The company plans to launch its first products with U.S. creators in late 2026 and has set an ambitious target of more than 200 creator-led software brands by 2030. For American influencers wondering what comes after the sponsorship era, that could make Affinity Labs a name worth knowing.

item.title: Elevation Capital Bets $10.5 Million That an AI-Powered Indian Studio Can Build Your Next Phone Game Obsession
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Spill Games raises $10.5M Series A led by Elevation Capital to scale its AI-led mobile game studio, Compass engine and casual puzzle titles worldwide.
item.content:encoded:
Bengaluru's Spill Games, maker of Cozy Finds and Zen Math Crossword, lands a Series A roughly six months after its seed round.

The next puzzle game eating up your commute may be coming out of Bengaluru, and it may have been tested, tuned and scaled with help from AI. Spill Games, a two-year-old mobile studio, has raised $10.5 million (about ₹100 crore) in a Series A round led by Elevation Capital.

Existing investors Centre Court Capital and PeerCapital also joined the round, Inc42 reported. The raise comes roughly six months after Spill closed a $3.1 million seed round in April, a fast follow-on that signals strong early traction.

An AI-Led, Portfolio-Driven Studio

Founded in 2024 by Om Misra, Tapan Ranjan and Harsh Garg, Spill builds free-to-play casual, puzzle and hybrid-casual titles for a global audience. Its portfolio includes Cozy Finds, Sticker by Number, Zen Math Crossword, Bird Rescue Jam and Grill Master, monetized through advertising and in-app purchases.

"We started Spill because we love making and playing games," Misra told DealStreetAsia. The business model, however, is built on discipline rather than passion alone. Spill launches games quickly to test assumptions, then uses player feedback and in-game data to decide which titles deserve more investment and which get cut.

The Compass Engine

At the center of that process is Compass, Spill's in-house engine that brings together tools for analytics, player retention, monetization and live operations. Because the infrastructure is reused across games, the studio says it can shorten development and testing cycles, targeting speeds roughly four times faster than traditional approaches.

That speed matters in casual mobile gaming, where hits are unpredictable and user acquisition costs can sink a studio that bets too heavily on any single title.

Built in India, Played in America

Spill is part of a new wave of Indian studios building for players overseas. At the time of its seed round, the company said about half of its users came from the United States, followed by Brazil and Japan. It previously set goals of testing more than 20 prototypes within 18 months and launching five to ten profitable titles.

The timing is notable. India's government has banned real-money gaming, pushing investor attention toward studios that earn money from ads and in-app purchases instead of wagers. Spill sits squarely in that safer lane.

Where the Money Goes

Spill plans to use the new capital to scale its existing games, expand its development pipeline, strengthen the AI and technology capabilities of Compass, acquire users and selectively grow its team.

For Elevation Capital, one of India's most active early-stage firms, the bet is that a data-driven studio can turn hit-making from luck into a repeatable system. If Spill pulls that off, the American players already making up half its audience will be the ones who notice first.

item.title: 5 Things to Know Before You Buy Rapid Rewards Points
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Before you buy Southwest Rapid Rewards points, learn five facts on pricing, real value, Companion Pass rules, limits, and cancellations.
item.content:encoded:
Southwest's points work differently from every other airline's. Five facts decide whether buying them helps you.

Disclosure: YourInfoDaily may earn a commission if you buy through links in this article. Offers change and are often targeted, so confirm the terms in your own account before buying.

Before you buy Rapid Rewards points, know these five things: your discount is personal, a point is worth about 1.3 cents, bought points don't count toward the Companion Pass, the purchase isn't airfare to your card, and point bookings are unusually easy to cancel. Together, they tell you when buying helps and when it doesn't.

1. Your discount is not the same as everyone else's

Southwest's standard price is 3 cents per point. It discounts points regularly, but not equally. One Mile at a Time reported that during a sale running September 2 to October 2, 2026, different members were offered 35%, 45%, or 50% off. Award Travel Finder's tracker, updated October 9, 2026, listed a 50% discount through October 29.

On a purchase of 60,000 points, those tiers look like this:

  • 50% off: $900, or 1.5 cents per point.
  • 45% off: $990, or 1.65 cents per point.
  • 35% off: $1,170, or 1.95 cents per point.

The discount in that sale applied only to purchases of at least 3,000 points in one transaction.

What to do: log in and look at your own offer before you read anyone's verdict on the sale, including this one. A 50% offer and a 35% offer lead to different answers.

2. A point is worth about 1.3 cents, almost every time

With most airlines, a point's value swings widely, and experts hunt for sweet spots. Southwest is different. Frequent Miler explains that award prices depend on demand and the flight's cash price, rising and falling with the fare. Any seat for sale can be booked with points.

The result is predictable value. Frequent Miler's benchmark is 1.3 cents per point. One Mile at a Time estimates 1.1 to 1.5 cents.

That predictability works against buyers. No hidden jackpot makes points bought at 1.5 cents suddenly worth 4 cents. One Mile at a Time concludes that buying at 1.5 cents or more rarely makes sense, because points usually redeem for less.

What to do: treat buying as a way to complete a booking, not as a discount on travel.

3. Bought points do not count toward the Companion Pass

The Companion Pass lets a named companion fly with you for only the taxes. Frequent Miler requires 135,000 qualifying points in a calendar year.

Purchased points do not qualify. Neither do points transferred from another member, most bonus points, or points transferred in from hotel partners or Chase Ultimate Rewards. What does count: base points from paid flights, Southwest credit card spending, card welcome bonuses, and many partner activities.

What to do: if the pass is your target, put your money into paid flights and card spending. Buy points only for redemptions.

See the Rapid Rewards offer on your account.

4. There are limits, and your card sees a different merchant

According to One Mile at a Time, you can buy up to 60,000 points per day, with no annual limit. That is unusually open. Most programs cap purchases annually.

The sale is processed by Points.com, not by Southwest. Your credit card will not record it as an airline purchase, so do not expect an airfare bonus category to apply. One Mile at a Time suggests using a card with a minimum spending requirement or one with strong everyday rewards.

What to do: choose a card for its base earning rate, and buy only what your booking needs. The lack of an annual cap isn't a reason to stock up.

5. Points bookings are easy to undo, and points never expire

This is the best argument for holding Rapid Rewards points at all.

  • Cancellations. Frequent Miler notes that you can cancel award flights for no fee up to 10 minutes before departure, with points returned immediately. One Mile at a Time adds that a canceled cash ticket becomes a travel credit for a future flight, while redeposited points can be used for anyone.
  • Changes. If your flight price drops after you book, Frequent Miler says changing to a cheaper fare returns the difference in points.
  • Expiration. Rapid Rewards points do not expire, and no activity is needed to keep them. Closing your account forfeits them.

What to do: if your travel dates are uncertain, a points booking gives you a clean exit. After you book, check the price again periodically. If it falls, rebook and collect the difference.

Top up your Rapid Rewards balance.

So when should you buy?

  • Buy when you are a few thousand points short of a flight you are ready to book. A 3,000-point top-up at 50% off costs about $45.
  • Consider buying when your plans may change, and you value getting points back more than holding a travel credit.
  • Do not buy to pay for a whole trip at a 35% or 45% discount, to chase the Companion Pass, or because a sale is ending. Another sale will follow.

A quick self-check

  • What discount does my account show?
  • What is the cash fare, and what is the points price?
  • How many points am I actually missing?
  • If I cancel, would I rather hold points or a travel credit?

Two more notes. Southwest offers a Cash + Points option, which Frequent Miler says yields poor value per point. And free checked bags now depend on your fare, elite status, or a Southwest credit card, so include bag costs when you compare a Southwest fare with a competitor's.

FAQ

How much are Rapid Rewards points worth?

About 1.3 cents each by Frequent Miler's benchmark, with a typical range of 1.1 to 1.5 cents.

Is there a limit on how many Southwest points you can buy?

Up to 60,000 per day, with no annual cap.

Do Rapid Rewards points expire?

No.

Can I get a refund on points I buy?

Treat purchases as final and read the terms shown at checkout before you pay.
